method_verbatim.value: PLE = PEEP − end-expiratory PES; ΔPL = (Plateau pressure − end-inspiratory PES) − (PEEP − end-expiratory PES)

provenance.quote: As recently reported27 we used the difference between airway opening pressure (PAW) and esophageal pressure (PES) at end expiration to calculate end-expiratory transpulmonary pressure (PLE), reflecting transpulmonary pressure (PL) in the middle to dependent regions of the lung: PLE = PEEP − end-expiratory PES ... To determine alveolar tidal stretch at each breath, driving PL was computed as: ΔPL = (Plateau pressure − end-inspiratory PES) − (PEEP − end-expiratory PES)
provenance.location: p. 793, Measurements

subgroup_flags.classification_notes: All 14 patients met Berlin ARDS criteria, so ards_subgroup=ards_only. Mean BMI 58.6 kg/m2, so obese_population. Study procedures started on average 1 day after initiation of mechanical ventilation, so timing_subgroup=early_within_48h. The intervention used esophageal balloon to target end-expiratory transpulmonary pressure 0-2 cmH2O (absolute positive end-expiratory ptp). The decremental PEEP strategy was based on best respiratory system elastance, not a transpulmonary pressure target.
